text:
li: Heads up — noticed a tail-latency regression in prod after the runtime change landed (8f4c2b). Perfetto flame diff shows a long stripe in the kernel selector hotpath around request batching.

michael: On it. Do you have the perfetto and nsys traces? Any obvious kernel-level hotspots?

li: Uploaded both: perfetto://pf-456 and nsys://trace123. Quick paste from perfetto flame (before -> after):\n```
before: kernel_selector: 8ms  | conv_kernel: 12ms | memcpy: 4ms
after:  kernel_selector: 28ms | conv_kernel: 14ms | memcpy: 18ms
```\nLooks like the selector time jumped and memcpy waits increased.

sasha: :eyes: Reproducer on microbench? Could be scheduler preemption/spin waiting on stream sync. I saw preempt events in `perf sched` aligned to the same timeframe on a canary run.

li: I ran `perf record -a -g -- sleep 30` on the canary and dumped `perf script`. Relevant snippet:\n```
kernel_selector() [4.2ms] -> schedule() preempt at 24ms -> cudaMemcpyAsync stalled until 42ms
```\nThat preempt window matches the perfetto stripe.

michael: CI bisect started to isolate the commit. @ci-bisect-bot any updates?

ci-bisect-bot: bisect job 7821 started. Candidate commits: 8f4c2b..9a7e1f. Running microbench suite `runtime/batching/selector`.

ci-bisect-bot: bisect result: regression introduced between 9a1d7a -> 9a7e1f. Culprit patch modifies kernel selection thresholds for short sequences.

li: Found the diff. The heuristic changed the sequence-length threshold from 32 -> 64 to prefer the 'conservative' conv kernel for small batches:\n```
- if (seq_len <= 32) choose_fast_conv();
+ if (seq_len <= 64) choose_conservative_conv();
```\nThis increases selector work and pushes more memcpy/stream syncs due to different launch patterns.

sasha: That explains it. Conservative kernel has extra setup and potentially different stream usage, causing preemption windows. Two options: revert, or adapt scheduler affinity and coalesce memcpy to avoid preemption spikes.

michael: Can we add a perf test and a canary rollout? I prefer a quick revert to restore SLOs, then follow up with a perf-safe rework.

li: I'll open PR to revert 9a7e1f and add a microbench that asserts selector median < 12ms for typical seq_len distribution. PR will include trace IDs and perf logs: `nsys:trace123`, `perfetto:pf-456`, `perf:perf-0912`.\n
sasha: Sounds good. Also add a test exercising preemption scenario: run on a 2-socket host with background load to catch the scheduler issue.

michael: Approved for revert. Please tag me in the PR and add the canary job. :thumbsup:

li: Roger. Pushing PR in 10m. Will monitor canary and post updated traces.
